env.world: A triangular array of finite-population conflict-graph experiments. For each \(n\) the population is \(\mathcal I_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with a known fixed simple undirected interference relation \(G_n\) on \(\mathcal I_n\), adjacency matrix \(A_{G_n}\), formal direct-effect conflict-graph operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), loop-inclusive spectral radius \(\lambda_n=1+\lambda_{\max}(A_{G_n})\ge1\), and closed maximum degree \(D_n=\max_i(1+\deg_{G_n}(i))\). Potential outcomes \(Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)\in\mathbb R\) are fixed numbers indexed by unit \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) and assignment \(\mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal I_n}\); there is no super-population sampling, and the endpoints are \(a_{n,i}=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf e_{n,i})\), \(b_{n,i}=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf 0_n)\), where \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) treats only \(i\) and \(\mathbf 0_n\) treats nobody. The only randomness is the family of independent desired-exposure coordinates \(U_{n,i}\in\{0,1,*\}\), taking the values \(1,0,*\) with probabilities \(p_n/2,p_n/2,t_n\), where \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\) and \(t_n=1-p_n\); \(\mathbb P_U\) and \(\mathbb E_U\) are the product law and expectation of these coordinates conditional on the fixed graph and potential outcomes. A unit-to-rank permutation \(\pi_n\) with inverse \(\rho_n\) fixes the reveal order and determines the strict earlier-neighbour sets \(B_{n,i}=\{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n,\ \pi_n(j)<\pi_n(i)\}\). The realized assignment \(Z_n\) is the fixed \(r=2\) conflict-graph-design output, so that on the endpoint-exposure event \(E_{n,i,k}=\{U_{n,i}=k,\ U_{n,\ell}=*\ \text{for every}\ \ell\in B_{n,i}\}\), of known probability \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\), the assignment agrees with \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) (when \(k=1\)) or with \(\mathbf 0_n\) (when \(k=0\)) on the closed \(G_n\)-neighbourhood of \(i\). The observed outcome is \(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{n,i}(Z_n)\), the target is the finite-population direct effect \(\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_i(a_{n,i}-b_{n,i})\), the estimator is \(T_n=n^{-1}\sum_iY_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\{\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,1})-\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,0})\}/q_{n,i}\) with contrast signs \(s_1=1,s_0=-1\), and its exact randomization variance and standard deviation are \(\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}_U(T_n)\) and \(\sigma_n\).

env.world: The forward reveal-order martingale world attached to the design of \(\mathrm S1\). The oriented adjacency matrix \(\mathsf P_n\) has \((\mathsf P_n)_{ji}=1\) exactly when \(j\in B_{n,i}\), so rows index earlier parents and columns later children. Each desired-exposure coordinate is split into its nonnull indicator \(R_{n,i}=\mathbf 1\{U_{n,i}\ne*\}\) and, on \(\{R_{n,i}=1\}\), an independent Rademacher label \(S_{n,i}\in\{-1,1\}\) encoding the values \(1\) and \(0\). The endpoint coefficients are \(\delta_{n,i}=a_{n,i}-b_{n,i}\), \(\gamma_{n,i}=a_{n,i}+b_{n,i}\), \(w_{n,i}=|a_{n,i}|+|b_{n,i}|\), with vectors \(w_n=(w_{n,i})_i\) and \(v_n=\lambda_nw_n+\mathsf P_nw_n\). The prefix weights are \(h_{n,i}=\prod_{\ell\in B_{n,i}}(1-R_{n,\ell})/t_n\) and its truncation \(h_{n,i,<s}=\prod_{\ell\in B_{n,i}:\pi_n(\ell)<s}(1-R_{n,\ell})/t_n\), both taking values in \([0,2]\). The raw sum is \(F_n=nT_n\), the rank-indexed filtration is \(\mathcal F_{n,0}=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\) and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\), and the rank-\(s\) predictable coefficients are \(J_{n,s}=\sum_{i:(\mathsf P_n)_{\rho_n(s),i}=1}\delta_{n,i}h_{n,i,<s}\), \(C_{n,s}=\delta_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n-J_{n,s}/t_n\), and \(G_{n,s}=\gamma_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n\). The Doob increment is \(M_{n,s}=\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s}]-\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), its predictable quadratic variation is \(Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), and \(\Delta_{n,s}Q_n\) is the signed difference of \(Q_n\) between \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=1\) and \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=0\) with all other reveal coordinates held fixed.

env.world: The observable spectral variance-bound and feasible-inference world. The signed exposure weights are \(W_{n,i,k}=s_k\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,k})/q_{n,i}\) for \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) and \(k\in\{0,1\}\), with known covariance matrix \(\mathbf V_n=\operatorname{Cov}_U((W_{n,i,k})_{i,k})\in\mathbb S_+^{2n}\) and largest eigenvalue \(L_n=\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf V_n)\). The endpoint second-moment mass is \(H_{2,n}=\sum_i(a_{n,i}^2+b_{n,i}^2)\), estimated by \(\widehat H_{2,n}=\sum_i\sum_k(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}})^2\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,k})/q_{n,i}\); the conservative spectral variance bound and its feasible version are \(\mathrm{VB}_n=L_nH_{2,n}/n^2\) and \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=L_n\widehat H_{2,n}/n^2\). Inference uses a fixed miscoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the normal quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)>0\) depending only on \(B\), \(c\) and \(\alpha\), and the feasible confidence set \(C_{n,\alpha}\), which is the Wald interval centred at \(T_n\) with half-width \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}\) when \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n>0\) and all of \(\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=0\).

env.world: The critical repeated-star boundary world. A boundary constant \(\beta>0\) is fixed; the critical star size is \(k_n=\lfloor\beta n^{2/3}\rfloor\) and the number of disjoint full stars is \(m_n=\lfloor n/(k_n+1)\rfloor\), the remaining vertices being isolated padding. The limiting intensity is \(r_{\beta}=(2\beta^{3/2})^{-1}\). The boundary law is the law \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\) of \(\sqrt{8/9}\,Z_0-(N_{r_{\beta}}-r_{\beta})/(3\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\), where \(Z_0\) is standard normal and \(N_{r_{\beta}}\) is a Poisson variable of mean \(r_{\beta}\) independent of \(Z_0\). It has variance one and third cumulant \(-1/(27\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\ne0\), so it is not \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
